# Parts

Building-block parts for the rare case where a component's props cannot express what you need. Prefer the props-first components.

Each part checks that it sits inside its root and, in development, throws a message with the JSX it belongs in.

## Field parts

The state owner of a field built from parts. It connects the label, description and error to the control, and passes `name`, `disabled` and `required` down. Use the `Field` component instead unless its props cannot express your layout; every Ouro form control is built on these parts. Parts link the description and error after hydration; use `Field` when the server HTML must carry them, or pass `id`s and `aria-describedby` yourself.

```tsx
import {
  FieldControl,
  FieldDescription,
  FieldError,
  FieldLabel,
  FieldRoot,
} from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/field/field-parts";
```

### Required nesting

```tsx
<FieldRoot name="email" required>
  <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
  <FieldDescription>We never share it.</FieldDescription>
  <FieldControl type="email" />
  <FieldError />
</FieldRoot>
```

Each part checks that it sits inside `<FieldRoot>`. Outside it, a part throws in development with a message that shows this JSX shape.

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `FieldControl` | The control, a text `<input>` by default. It takes the field's id, `name`, `disabled` and `required`, `aria-invalid` from its error, and `aria-describedby` from its description and error. Render another element with `render={<textarea />}`. |
| `FieldDescription` | Supporting text for the control, read after its label through `aria-describedby`. |
| `FieldError` | The error message, linked to the control through `aria-describedby`. Without children it shows the browser's validation message, or a Base UI `Form` error for the field's `name`; with `match` and children it always shows them. It fades and slides in. |
| `FieldLabel` | The control's label. It points at the control by id. A required field shows a marker after it, drawn by CSS on the element around the label, so the label's text and the control's name stay exactly what you wrote (screen readers hear "required" from the control). `className` goes on that element; hide the label visually with `className="sr-only"`. |
| `FieldRoot` | The state owner of a field built from parts. It connects the label, description and error to the control, and passes `name`, `disabled` and `required` down. Use the `Field` component instead unless its props cannot express your layout; every Ouro form control is built on these parts. Parts link the description and error after hydration; use `Field` when the server HTML must carry them, or pass `id`s and `aria-describedby` yourself. |

## Select parts

Children of `<Select>`, for what its props cannot express.

```tsx
import {
  SelectGroup,
  SelectItem,
} from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/select/select-parts";
```

### Required nesting

```tsx
<Select label="Produce" name="produce">
  <SelectGroup label="Fruit">
    <SelectItem value="apple">Apple</SelectItem>
  </SelectGroup>
</Select>
```

Each part checks that it sits inside `<Select>`. Outside it, a part throws in development with a message that shows this JSX shape.

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `SelectGroup` | A labeled group of `SelectItem`s. With `options`, pass a group as `{ label: "Fruit", options: [...] }` instead. |
| `SelectItem` | One option in a `Select`, for options that need more than text (an icon, a color swatch). Pass `options` to `Select` instead when every option is text; it renders these for you. |

## Dialog parts

The state owner of a centered dialog built from parts. Use the `Dialog` component instead unless its props cannot express your layout; `Dialog` also becomes a bottom sheet on phones, which parts do not.

```tsx
import {
  DialogBackdrop,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogPopup,
  DialogPortal,
  DialogRoot,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
  DialogViewport,
} from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/dialog/dialog-parts";
```

### Required nesting

```tsx
<DialogRoot>
  <DialogTrigger render={<Button>Edit</Button>} />
  <DialogPortal>
    <DialogBackdrop />
    <DialogViewport>
      <DialogPopup size="sm">
        <DialogTitle>Edit recipe</DialogTitle>
        <DialogContent>…</DialogContent>
        <DialogFooter>
          <DialogClose render={<Button>Done</Button>} />
        </DialogFooter>
      </DialogPopup>
    </DialogViewport>
  </DialogPortal>
</DialogRoot>
```

Each part checks that it sits inside `<DialogRoot>`. Outside it, a part throws in development with a message that shows this JSX shape.

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `DialogBackdrop` | The dimming layer behind the dialog. On iOS it stays anchored to the top of the screen on a scrolled page. A `ref` reaches the backdrop element. |
| `DialogClose` | Closes the dialog. Pass your button as `render={<Button>Done</Button>}`. |
| `DialogContent` | The dialog's body. It scrolls when the dialog is taller than the screen, and while it overflows it is a tab stop, so a keyboard can scroll it. |
| `DialogDescription` | A line under the title that describes the dialog. |
| `DialogFooter` | The actions row. A row at the end on wider screens; on phones the actions stack full width. Put the primary action last, so it sits at the bottom on phones, nearest the thumb. |
| `DialogPopup` | The dialog panel. It scales up from 0.96 and fades in over 300ms, and scales and fades out in 200ms; reduced motion keeps only the fade. |
| `DialogPortal` | Moves the dialog to the end of `<body>`, in its own stacking context at the `--ouro-layer` z-index (50 by default, from ouro-base.css). If your app has fixed bars above z-50, raise it in a `:root` rule of your own after the Ouro tokens, outside any `@layer`: `:root { --ouro-layer: 60; }`. Don't edit the line shadcn wrote; `shadcn add` resets it. |
| `DialogRoot` | The state owner of a centered dialog built from parts. Use the `Dialog` component instead unless its props cannot express your layout; `Dialog` also becomes a bottom sheet on phones, which parts do not. |
| `DialogTitle` | The dialog's title, which names it. Every dialog needs one. |
| `DialogTrigger` | The button that opens the dialog. Pass your button as `render={<Button>Open</Button>}`. |
| `DialogViewport` | The full-screen layer that centers the popup and keeps it clear of the screen edges. |

## Popover parts

The state owner of a popover built from parts. Use the `Popover` component instead unless its props cannot express your layout; `Popover` also becomes a bottom sheet on phones with `presentation="auto"`, which parts do not.

```tsx
import {
  PopoverClose,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverPopup,
  PopoverPortal,
  PopoverPositioner,
  PopoverRoot,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/popover/popover-parts";
```

### Required nesting

```tsx
<PopoverRoot>
  <PopoverTrigger render={<Button>Share</Button>} />
  <PopoverPortal>
    <PopoverPositioner side="bottom" align="start">
      <PopoverPopup>
        <PopoverTitle>Share recipe</PopoverTitle>
        …
      </PopoverPopup>
    </PopoverPositioner>
  </PopoverPortal>
</PopoverRoot>
```

Each part checks that it sits inside `<PopoverRoot>`. Outside it, a part throws in development with a message that shows this JSX shape.

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `PopoverClose` | Closes the popover. Pass your button as `render={<Button>Done</Button>}`. With no `render` it is the screen-reader close button `Popover` uses: hidden until it has keyboard focus, so phone screen-reader users, who have no Escape key, can close it. |
| `PopoverDescription` | A line under the title that describes the popover. |
| `PopoverPopup` | The popover panel, 18rem wide (never wider than the screen allows) with 1rem of padding. It grows from the trigger over 200ms on the ease-out token and fades; reduced motion keeps only the fade. Put a `PopoverTitle` first: it names the popover. |
| `PopoverPortal` | Moves the popover to the end of `<body>`, in its own stacking context at the `--ouro-layer` z-index (50 by default, from ouro-base.css), like Dialog and Sheet. Raise it in a `:root` rule of your own after the Ouro tokens: `:root { --ouro-layer: 60; }`. |
| `PopoverPositioner` | Places the popover beside its trigger (or `anchor`), 8px away and at least 8px from the screen edges, and flips it to the other side when there is no room. |
| `PopoverRoot` | The state owner of a popover built from parts. Use the `Popover` component instead unless its props cannot express your layout; `Popover` also becomes a bottom sheet on phones with `presentation="auto"`, which parts do not. |
| `PopoverTitle` | The popover's title, which names it. Every popover needs one. |
| `PopoverTrigger` | The button that opens and closes the popover. Pass your button as `render={<Button>Open</Button>}`. The trigger anchors the popover, which opens on click while the button is pressed, so the press scale is cancelled on it (Button's pressed wash still shows) and the popover lands once. |

## Sheet parts

The state owner of a sheet built from parts. Use the `Sheet` component instead unless its props cannot express your layout.

```tsx
import {
  SheetBackdrop,
  SheetClose,
  SheetContent,
  SheetDescription,
  SheetHandle,
  SheetPopup,
  SheetPortal,
  SheetRoot,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetTrigger,
  SheetViewport,
} from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/sheet/sheet-parts";
```

### Required nesting

```tsx
<SheetRoot side="bottom">
  <SheetTrigger render={<Button>Open</Button>} />
  <SheetPortal>
    <SheetBackdrop />
    <SheetViewport>
      <SheetPopup>
        <SheetHandle />
        <SheetTitle>Filters</SheetTitle>
        <SheetContent>…</SheetContent>
      </SheetPopup>
    </SheetViewport>
  </SheetPortal>
</SheetRoot>
```

Each part checks that it sits inside `<SheetRoot>`. Outside it, a part throws in development with a message that shows this JSX shape.

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `SheetBackdrop` | The dimming layer. It lightens as the sheet is dragged away. On iOS it stays anchored to the top of the screen on a scrolled page. A `ref` reaches the backdrop element. |
| `SheetClose` | Closes the sheet. Pass your button as `render={<Button>Done</Button>}`. |
| `SheetContent` | The scrollable body. A mouse can select text in it without dragging the sheet; touch still drags from anywhere once the body is scrolled to the top. While it overflows it is a tab stop, so a keyboard can scroll it. |
| `SheetDescription` | A line under the title that describes the dialog. |
| `SheetHandle` | The grab handle at the free edge of a bottom or top sheet. Decorative; renders nothing on side sheets. |
| `SheetPopup` | The sheet panel. It stretches past its edge when pulled and springs back on release. |
| `SheetPortal` | Moves the sheet to the end of `<body>` and makes it aware of the software keyboard (`Drawer.VirtualKeyboardProvider`), so focused inputs stay visible. The portal is its own stacking context at the `--ouro-layer` z-index (50 by default, from ouro-base.css). If your app has fixed bars above z-50, raise it in a `:root` rule of your own after the Ouro tokens, outside any `@layer`: `:root { --ouro-layer: 60; }`. Don't edit the line shadcn wrote; `shadcn add` resets it. |
| `SheetRoot` | The state owner of a sheet built from parts. Use the `Sheet` component instead unless its props cannot express your layout. |
| `SheetTitle` | The sheet's title, which names the dialog. Every sheet needs one. |
| `SheetTrigger` | The button that opens the sheet. Pass your button as `render={<Button>Open</Button>}`. |
| `SheetViewport` | The full-screen layer that positions the popup against its edge. |

## Tabs parts

The state owner of tabs built from parts. Use the `Tabs` component instead unless its `items` cannot express your layout, such as a tab that holds a badge next to its label or a panel shared by two tabs.

```tsx
import {
  TabsIndicator,
  TabsList,
  TabsPanel,
  TabsRoot,
  TabsTab,
} from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/tabs/tabs-parts";
```

### Required nesting

```tsx
<TabsRoot defaultValue="ingredients">
  <TabsList aria-label="Recipe">
    <TabsTab value="ingredients">Ingredients</TabsTab>
    <TabsTab value="method">Method</TabsTab>
    <TabsIndicator />
  </TabsList>
  <TabsPanel value="ingredients">…</TabsPanel>
  <TabsPanel value="method">…</TabsPanel>
</TabsRoot>
```

Each part checks that it sits inside `<TabsRoot>`. Outside it, a part throws in development with a message that shows this JSX shape.

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `TabsIndicator` | The line that slides to the selected tab. Put it last inside `TabsList`. |
| `TabsList` | The row (or column) of tabs. Name it with `aria-label` when the page has more than one set of tabs. `activateOnFocus` selects a tab when the arrow keys focus it. A row that scrolls, on a phone, fades out on the side that hides more tabs. |
| `TabsPanel` | The content shown while the tab with the same `value` is selected. |
| `TabsRoot` | The state owner of tabs built from parts. Use the `Tabs` component instead unless its `items` cannot express your layout, such as a tab that holds a badge next to its label or a panel shared by two tabs. |
| `TabsTab` | One tab, a button that shows the panel with the same `value`. |

## Table parts

The root of a table built from parts, with its caption and its scrolling region. `Table` takes the same parts as children (`<Table caption="Pantry">…</Table>`), so use it instead unless you are composing parts of your own; `Table` also builds the whole table from `columns` and `rows`.

```tsx
import {
  TableBody,
  TableCell,
  TableFooter,
  TableHead,
  TableHeader,
  TableRoot,
  TableRow,
} from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/table/table-parts";
```

### Required nesting

```tsx
<TableRoot caption="Pantry">
  <TableHeader>
    <TableRow>
      <TableHead>Item</TableHead>
      <TableHead align="end">Qty</TableHead>
    </TableRow>
  </TableHeader>
  <TableBody>
    <TableRow href="/pantry/flour">
      <TableCell rowHeader>Flour</TableCell>
      <TableCell align="end">2 kg</TableCell>
    </TableRow>
  </TableBody>
</TableRoot>
```

Each part checks that it sits inside `<TableRoot>`. Outside it, a part throws in development with a message that shows this JSX shape.

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `TableBody` | The table's body rows (`<tbody>`). |
| `TableCell` | A cell (`<td>`), or the row's header with `rowHeader` (`<th scope="row">`). |
| `TableFooter` | Summary rows under the body (`<tfoot>`), such as a total, with a line above them. |
| `TableHead` | A column header (`<th scope="col">`) in a `TableHeader` row. |
| `TableHeader` | The table's header rows (`<thead>`), holding a `TableRow` of `TableHead` cells. With `stickyHeader` on the Table, they stay at the top while the rows scroll. |
| `TableRoot` | The root of a table built from parts, with its caption and its scrolling region. `Table` takes the same parts as children (`<Table caption="Pantry">…</Table>`), so use it instead unless you are composing parts of your own; `Table` also builds the whole table from `columns` and `rows`. |
| `TableRow` | One row (`<tr>`). With `href` a body row is one link, held by its row header cell. |
